full_judgment: 4. Petitioner having not stated as to how and under what authority he was appointed Mutawalli we directed the learned Advocate for the respondent Nos. 2 and 3 to produce the relevant file and the same was duly produced at the time of hearing of the Rule. Petitioner also filed as affidavit-in-reply. We have perused the file of HC No. 11278, petition, affidavit-in-opposition, affidavit-in-reply and other relevant papers and on consideration of the same along with order sheet of SC Case No. 11278 we find that the waqf in question was enrolled for the first time by order dated 29-11-47 and one Abdul Hafiz, son of Samiruddin, was appointed Mutawalli. Admittedly, there is no waqf deed and in the CS Khatian property of the said waqf was recorded as a Lakheraj waqf property under the Dhaka Nawab Court of Wards Estate showing Nawab Khwaja Salimullah as Mutawalli. It appears that Samiruddin, grandfather of the petitioner, was Khadem of the Mazar situated in the waqf property. Subsequently, in his order dated 28-8-48 Commissioner of Waqfs observed that as per CS Khatian Nawab Khwaja Salimullah was Mutawalli and father of Bashiruddin and Abdul Hafiz was the Khadem. Subsequently, by order dated 18-5-49 Commissioner of Waqfs declared Nawab Habibullah Bahadur as Mutwalli and vacated his earlier order dated 29-11-47 appointing Abdul Hafiz as the Mutwalli and by order dated 29-1-50 Nawab Bahadur was appointed Mutwalli. Subsequently by order dated 31-12-56 Bashiruddin was appointed as ad-interim Mutwalli under section 40 of the Bengal Waqfs Act, 1934 until further orders or till the order is set aside by a Court of competent jurisdiction. The said Mutwalli at the advanced state of his age on 4-12-79 filed an application for appointing his eldest son the petitioner as the mutwalli, Thereafter he having died on 17-12-79 his son present petitioner was substituted as mutwalli on 22-12-79.
